gapThisFills: One of the four genuine-gap checklist acquisitions ordered by Drew 2026-09-28. Cell 2024|bowman-chrome carries 24,422 unbacked sales (raw census label: 'mixed: N-number-resolve + checklist ingest (Bowman's Best/CPA insert)'); the orchestrator-confirmed SPECIFIC gap this package targets is that no year of 2024 Bowman's Best had ever had a numbered BASE checklist acquired -- only parallels vocabulary and a Beckett variations guide existed prior to this package. This base checklist unlocks matching for the product's own base-card sales (both the 70-card veterans/rookies range #1-70 and the 30-card Top Prospects range TP-1..TP-30); it does NOT by itself resolve every unbacked sale at the 2024|bowman-chrome cell, since that cell is a distinct, already-registered sibling product (bowman-chrome) and some of its unbacked volume is CPA-insert/autograph rows outside this base-only scope. Held-out auto/insert/parallel subsets (see heldOut below) remain unbacked after this package and are explicitly not claimed as fixed by it.
sourcePageShape: Beckett xlsx workbook, sheets include Base, Autographs, Inserts (standard Beckett shape, same converter used by every other package in this family). The Base sheet's own numbering states two ranges as printed on the actual cards: cards #1-70 for the base veterans/rookies portion (Mike Trout, Ronald Acuna Jr., Jackson Holliday, Paul Skenes, Bo Bichette, etc.), and cards TP-1 through TP-30 for the Top Prospects portion (Jose Perdomo, Roman Anthony, Jacob Wilson, Dylan Crews, etc.) -- a distinct printed number prefix, not a continuation of 71-100. Base cards also carry 16 named Refractor-family parallel rungs (Refractors, Wave Refractors, Superfractors, Red/Red Lava/Purple/Purple Mojo/Orange/Green/Gold/Gold Lava/Blue/Blue X-Fractors/Black/Aqua Lava/Yellow Lazer Refractors) plus Mini-Diamond(s) Refractor variants scoped to only part of the 100-card run -- all held out of this package, see heldOut below.
converterNote: Converted with the sanctioned scripts/convertBeckettChecklistXlsx.cjs (--xlsx <path> --year 2024 --set-key bowmans-best --set-name "2024 Bowman's Best" --sport baseball --out 2024-bowmans-best-baseball.raw.csv --source-url <sourceUrl> --source-label beckett-s3-2026-09-28). Converter output: wrote 2024-bowmans-best-baseball.raw.csv; rows=4538 (deduped 0); by kind: {"base":1900,"auto":2145,"insert":493}; sections: 20 (anchors 2, parallels 0, own-cards 18). This committed CSV is filtered from that raw output down to only rows with category=base AND a blank parallel column -- the 100 plain-numbered base/prospects cards -- via: awk -F',' 'NR==1{print;next} $1=="base" && $3==""{print}' 2024-bowmans-best-baseball.raw.csv > 2024-bowmans-best-baseball.csv (fields re-ordered to the canonical header; parallel column left blank rather than "Base", matching sibling packages' convention).
categoryNote: Both ranges are staged under category=base (never a separate insert-/auto- category). Verified against the sanctioned ingester's own planStagedDirectory: with a single plain category, the TP- prefix already keeps every id distinct from the 1-70 range (no card-number collision, since 'TP-1' and '1' slugify to different cardNumbers), so planStagedDirectory measures zero need for subset separation and every one of the 100 rows resolves onto the plain bowmans-best setKey -- 100 staged rows, 100 distinct ids, 0 collisions, 0 unregistered keys. Splitting Top Prospects into its own insert-top-prospects category (the 1985 Donruss precedent's convention for a subset with a genuinely separate, colliding numbering track) was considered and rejected here: TP- already disambiguates on its own, and minting a second setKey (bowmans-best-top-prospects) for cards that are still fundamentally base-style chrome cards of the same product would fork one pool into two for no addressing reason -- the opposite of 'one card, one row, one pool.'
